facts.raw_span: paroxysmal chest pain
The chest pain had occurred 5 times during the day, and each episode lasted 15 to 30 minutes
blood pressure and pulse rate were 106/52 mm Hg and 64 beats per minutes
normal breath and heart sounds with no murmurs
Hemogram, serum electrolyte levels, kidney and liver function tests, B-type natriuretic peptide and D-dimer levels were all within normal limits
Cardiac troponin I level was 25 ng/mL (normal, <0.023 ng/mL)
sinus rhythm, ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR, Q wave in lead III, and ST-segment depression in leads I, II, aVL, aVF, and V2 to V6
sinus bradycardia (46 beats per minute), Q-wave amplitude deepening, ST-segment falling back to equipotential line, and T-wave inversion in lead III
total occlusion of the right coronary artery (RCA) and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery (LMCA)

concepts.why: The patient presented with paroxysmal chest pain, elevated cardiac troponin I level, and ECG changes consistent with myocardial infarction, including ST-segment elevation and Q waves.
The patient's ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR, consistent with STEMI.
The patient's ECG showed ST-segment depression and T-wave inversion, consistent with NSTEMI.
The patient's coronary angiography showed total occlusion of the right coronary artery and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery.
The patient presented with chest pain and ECG changes consistent with cardiac ischemia.

rationales.F01: Paroxysmal chest pain is a common symptom of myocardial infarction and cardiac ischemia.
rationales.F06: Elevated cardiac troponin I level is a strong indicator of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F07: ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR is a characteristic ECG finding in STEMI.
rationales.F09: Total occlusion of the right coronary artery and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery are indicative of coronary artery occlusion and myocardial infarction.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's ECG findings, including ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR, and the elevated cardiac troponin I level, are consistent with STEMI, which is a subtype of acute myocardial infarction.
